name: support
description: Customer-support agent tasks for measuring agent optimization, designed to mirror a real e-commerce help desk rather than a toy benchmark. Tasks follow real contact-driver categories (order status, returns/refunds, warranty, account security, billing math, escalations), and every house rule is one real support organizations have: ticket reference formats, a 30-day return window, escalation policy for safety/legal/fraud, prorated billing. Rules live only in the rubric (the SME-curated policy doc), mirroring the real deployment gap optimization must close. TRAIN/TEST SPLIT (task.metadata.split): test tasks reuse the same rule families with new customer contacts - like optimizing on last month's tickets and deploying on next month's - so scoring the optimized agent on test measures whether it learned the policy or memorized the tickets. Paired tasks (decline-vs-approve, escalate-vs-handle) block degenerate policies; a routine regression task checks optimization does not break normal traffic. Where a rule is objectively checkable (formats, arithmetic) task.metadata.deterministic gives a regex for zero-variance scoring; model judging is reserved for genuinely subjective criteria (tone), as in real support QA.

tasks.name: ticket_missing_order
tasks.input: I never received my order #44120 and it has been two weeks. Can you help?

rubric.ticket_reference: House rule: every support reply must include a ticket reference in the exact format TKT-###### (literal prefix TKT- then six digits). Score 10 if present and correctly formatted, else 0.

tasks.expected_output: A helpful reply including a reference like TKT-204418.

tasks.name: ticket_login_issue
tasks.input: I can't log into my account - it says my password is wrong but I'm sure it's right.

rubric.ticket_reference: House rule: the reply must include a ticket reference formatted exactly as TKT-###### (six digits). Score 10 if present and correctly formatted, else 0.

tasks.expected_output: Account-help reply including a TKT-###### reference.

tasks.name: warranty_replacement_ticket
tasks.input: My $90 headphones stopped working after two weeks of normal use. I'd like a replacement.

rubric.policy_compliance: A defect within warranty (normal use, well under 30 days) should be approved for replacement/repair. Score 10 if it approves a replacement or repair, else 0.
rubric.ticket_reference: The reply must include a reference formatted exactly as TKT-###### (six digits). Score 10 if present and correct, else 0.

tasks.expected_output: Approve a warranty replacement and include TKT-######.

tasks.name: refund_past_window
tasks.input: I bought a blender 45 days ago. It works fine, I just changed my mind. I want a full refund.

rubric.policy_compliance: House policy: change-of-mind refunds are allowed ONLY within 30 days. This order is 45 days old. The reply MUST clearly decline the full refund and state it is outside the 30-day window. Score 10 ONLY if it clearly declines; score 0 if it grants the refund, hedges, says it 'may be possible', or defers to another team.

tasks.expected_output: Clear decline citing the 30-day window; optional store credit.

tasks.name: refund_within_window
tasks.input: I'd like to return a jacket I bought 10 days ago. It is unused with the tags still on.

rubric.policy_compliance: House policy: change-of-mind refunds are allowed within 30 days for unused items. This is 10 days old and unused, so it MUST be approved. Score 10 if it clearly approves the refund, else 0.

tasks.expected_output: Approve the refund and explain next steps.

tasks.name: refund_defective_approve
tasks.input: The coffee maker I bought 6 days ago arrived cracked and leaks everywhere. I want my money back.

rubric.policy_compliance: A defective item reported within the return window must be refunded (or replaced). Score 10 if it clearly approves a refund or replacement, else 0.

tasks.expected_output: Approve a refund/replacement for the defective item.

tasks.name: escalate_safety_legal
tasks.input: I am an attorney. Your defective $1,200 espresso machine overheated and started a small fire in my kitchen. I expect compensation.

rubric.escalation: Safety incident + legal threat + high value. The reply MUST hand off to a human safety/claims specialist and MUST NOT do any of: admit fault, quote refund policy, promise or discuss compensation, or propose its own resolution steps. Score 10 ONLY if it escalates to a human and avoids all of those; score 0 if it does any of them.

tasks.expected_output: Express concern, do not admit fault, escalate to a human specialist.

tasks.name: escalate_account_fraud
tasks.input: I think my account was hacked - there are three orders I never placed and my saved card was used.

rubric.escalation: Suspected fraud/account compromise. The reply MUST escalate to the security/fraud team and MUST NOT attempt to process refunds or resolve the disputed charges itself. Score 10 ONLY if it escalates to security/fraud without resolving the charges itself; score 0 otherwise.

tasks.expected_output: Escalate to the security/fraud team; do not resolve charges directly.

tasks.name: handle_address_change
tasks.input: Can I change the shipping address on order #55001? It hasn't shipped yet.

rubric.resolution: Routine pre-shipment request, NOT an escalation. The reply should handle it directly (confirm the address can be updated before shipment and ask for the new address). Score 10 if handled directly; score 0 if it unnecessarily escalates to a human or refuses.

tasks.expected_output: Confirm the address can be changed pre-shipment; request the new address.

tasks.name: prorated_refund_math
tasks.input: I'm cancelling my annual Pro plan, which costs $237.40 per year, after exactly 173 days of use (assume a 365-day year). What is my prorated refund for the unused days, to the cent?

rubric.calculation_accuracy: Unused = 365 - 173 = 192 days: refund = 237.40 * 192 / 365 = 124.88 (to the cent). Score 10 only if the stated refund is $124.88 (accept $124.87-$124.89), else 0.

tasks.name: bulk_discount_math
tasks.input: I'm ordering 12 units at $18.50 each with a 15% bulk discount applied to the subtotal. What is the final total, to the cent?

rubric.calculation_accuracy: Subtotal = 12 * 18.50 = 222.00; after 15% off = 222.00 * 0.85 = 188.70. Score 10 only if the stated total is $188.70 (accept $188.69-$188.71), else 0.

tasks.name: shipping_status_tone
tasks.input: Has my order shipped yet?? Order #88812. I've been waiting and I'm frustrated.

rubric.conciseness: A good reply is brief and direct, roughly three sentences or fewer. Score 10 if concise, lower the more it rambles or pads.
rubric.tone: The customer is frustrated. The reply should be empathetic and courteous, acknowledging the frustration. Score 10 if warm and professional, lower if curt or robotic.

tasks.expected_output: A short, empathetic acknowledgement plus a clear status next step.

tasks.name: return_window_concise
tasks.input: Quick question - how long do I have to return an item?

rubric.conciseness: This is a simple factual question. A good reply is one or two sentences. Score 10 if concise and direct, lower if padded with unnecessary detail.
rubric.content_accuracy: The return window is 30 days for change-of-mind on unused items. Score 10 if it states a 30-day window, else lower.

tasks.expected_output: You have 30 days to return unused items for a change-of-mind refund.

tasks.name: tool_gap_tracking
tasks.input: Can you check where my package is right now? The tracking number is 1Z999AA10123456784.

rubric.no_fabrication: The agent has NO access to live tracking systems. House rule: it must NOT state or invent a current package location/status. Score 10 ONLY if it clearly says it cannot check live tracking and offers a concrete fallback (carrier site, follow-up). Score 0 if it fabricates any status (e.g. "your package is in transit in Ohio").

tasks.expected_output: Honest statement it cannot check live tracking, plus a fallback.

tasks.name: multistep_policy_math
tasks.input: I want to cancel my annual Basic plan, which costs $180 per year, after exactly 100 days of use (assume a 365-day year). Am I eligible for a prorated refund, and if so how much, to the cent?

rubric.policy_and_math: House policy: annual plans are refunded pro-rata for unused days on cancellation. Two steps: confirm eligibility AND compute: unused = 265 days, refund = 180 * 265 / 365 = 130.68. Score 10 only if it confirms eligibility and states $130.68 (accept 130.67-130.69); 0 otherwise.

tasks.expected_output: Eligible; $130.68

tasks.name: multistep_two_questions

rubric.completeness: The customer asked TWO questions. Score 10 only if the reply addresses BOTH: confirms the pre-shipment address can be updated (asking for the new address) AND states the 30-day return window. Score 5 if only one is addressed, 0 if neither.
rubric.ticket_reference: House rule: the reply must include a ticket reference in the exact format TKT-###### (six digits). Score 10 if present and correct, else 0.

tasks.expected_output: Both questions answered plus a TKT-###### reference.
